README: A whole-piece reading: every mark an edition prints for one fugue, in every voice and bar, attached to the game's own notes.

Notes are addressed as in data/touch/pieces.json: v = voice index (here 0 Soprano, 1 Alto, 2 Bass, pieces.json voiceNames), on = onset tick (tpq 1920; a 4/4 bar is 7680 ticks; bar n starts at (n-1)*7680). p (MIDI) and name are a check (names are the game's spelling, even where the edition renotates), bar and pos (sixteenths from the barline) are for people.

marks[]: one note's articulation. art is one of staccato (dot), wedge (Keil: shorter and sharper), tenuto (dash: full value, a slight lean), portato (dash over dot: held a little apart, each note weighted), accent (>), marcato (^ over a dot: struck hard and left), fermata. A note may have two marks (wedge+tenuto).

slurs[]: spans in one voice, from and to both included. kind "slur" = a group played as one gesture (joined inside, the last note lighter and, with lastShort, let go early); kind "portato" = dots under a slur (each note detached a little but carried in one line); kind "phrase" = a long phrasing arc over a whole subject or line. role says what the slur covers.
dyn[]: a printed level at a time, for the voices it was printed for (Busoni prints dynamics per staff, sometimes per voice).

hairpins[]: cresc/dim spans in time for the given voices. text[]: words printed in the score with an English gloss. tempo.changes[] is left empty on purpose: the owner has ruled out tempo warping except at fermatas, so Busoni's tempo words are kept only in tempo.notes[] (applied: false) and fermatas stay in marks[].

breaths[]: a printed caesura before a note. voicing[]: pianistic re-voicings, recorded as notes only and not to be applied: octave-doubling (interval in semitones) and added notes. ornaments[]: a printed ornament and how Busoni realises it.
rules[]: instructions that apply to unmarked notes; the game must apply these by rule. sections[]: Busoni's double bars.
fingering: a summary of patterns and a few samples (fingers in the order of the notes from that note on); not every digit is transcribed.
footnotes[]: German text (as printed, old spelling kept) and an English translation.
conf on every item: sure (clearly printed and placed), likely (printed, the placement or the sign read from a 300 dpi scan with some doubt), unsure (a guess: hard to see, or inferred).
This format is a superset of docs/wtc/readings/*.json: the old per-note subject marks can be derived from marks[] and slurs[] on the first entry.
title: Fugue 19 in A major, BWV 864

edition.author: Ferruccio B. Busoni
edition.title: Das wohltemperirte Clavier, Erster Theil, bearbeitet, erläutert und mit daran anknüpfenden Beispielen und Anweisungen für das Studium der modernen Clavierspieltechnik herausgegeben

character: Supple and gentle ("geschmeidig"; NB I: a "velvety flexibility", not to shy from its "femininity"); legato and even throughout.
dynamicPlan: sotto voce dolcemente (b.1), sempre legato, sempre egualmente (b.9); poco marc. bass (b.13); poco cresc. to più pieno (b.16–18), dim. to p (b.19–20), non cresc. (b.21); dolce, scorrevolmente (b.23); marc. alto (b.31); small swells (b.36–37); cresc. (b.40) to più f (b.42); dim. con affabilità (b.48); Coda dolce (b.49), espress. alto (b.52), fermata.

text.en: with friendliness (poco slentando, a tempo word, ignored)

rules.art: first eighth tenuto (never a sforzato, footnote 1); the rest of the subject legato under one arc
legato, even (sempre legato b.3, sempre egualmente b.9)

sections.en: development (footnote 3: a calm part, then a moving one)
third part (footnote 4: back in A major)

ornaments.name: G#4
ornaments.realisation: trill, realised in small notes above the staff (from the upper note, closing with the written turn F♯–G♯); exact count not legible

ornaments.name: D#5
ornaments.realisation: trill on the D♯ quarter, no realisation printed

ornaments.name: B4
ornaments.sign: small notes (turn or trill) above the B
ornaments.realisation: printed in small notes above the staff; not legible at 200 dpi

ornamentsNote: Two trills (b.8, b.26) and a small-note ornament (b.51); realisations printed in small notes are not legible at 200 dpi.

summary: Not transcribed: fingerings were skipped on purpose (gameplay does not use them).

footnotes.de: Von dem groben „Sforzato“ auf dem ersten Achtel des Themas, wie es die meisten Ausgaben „treu nach Czerny“ vorzeichnen, fehlt bei Bach jede Spur.
footnotes.en: No sforzato on the subject’s first eighth (Czerny’s accent is not Bach’s).

caveats: Economical pass: playing marks only. Fingerings, ossias ("oder", b.4, b.30) and tempo words (un poco allarg. b.19, a tempo b.20/49, poco slentando b.48) are left out; there is no ending slowing word.
Read from 200 dpi greyscale crops, one system at a time. Subject marks are generated from pieces.json entries[] using the template Busoni prints at b.1–6.
Footnotes 2–5 and NB II are structural (voice assignment, form, the g♯ reading, links with Book II) and left out.
notes: Game import (WTC 1.90, D392): "Tranquillo e piacevole. geschmeidig (flexibly)" (bar 1) kept as "Tranquillo e piacevole. geschmeidig": the gloss and footnote reference were the transcriber's, not printed words.
Game import (WTC 1.90, D392): "più pieno (fuller)" (bar 18) kept as "più pieno": the gloss and footnote reference were the transcriber's, not printed words.
